facts.text: Valatie’s name comes from the Dutch word “Vaaltje,” meaning little falls, a nod to the waterfalls that once powered nine cotton mills.
The village’s first post office opened in 1832, marking the start of Valatie’s long‑standing role as a local hub.
Valatie’s Main Street is famous for its three waterfalls—Valatie Kill Falls, Beaver Mill Falls, and Kinderhook Creek—each a historic landmark.
In 1946, fifteen village veterans founded the first Santa Claus Club in the United States, a tradition that still brings holiday cheer to Valatie.
The village’s Opera House began as a Presbyterian church in 1835 before becoming a public hall, reflecting Valatie’s adaptive reuse of historic buildings.
Harry Houdini filmed scenes of his last movie, “Haldane of the Secret Service,” at the base of Beaver Kill Falls in 1921, linking Valatie to early Hollywood history.
